assigned_keyword.operational_meaning: Mid-century atomic-age retrofuturism expressed through streamlined industrial forms, analog nuclear science hardware, enamel, Bakelite, chrome, bubble-era space equipment, and optimistic technology with a faintly uncanny edge.

frozen_concept.title: Night Shift at the Isotope Orchard
frozen_concept.subject: One unmistakably adult woman working as an isotope horticulturist.
frozen_concept.setting: A decommissioned 1962 reactor greenhouse converted into a hydroponic isotope orchard.
frozen_concept.event: She calibrates a chrome seed-vault while a compact analog robot presents a glowing fruit specimen in articulated tongs.

reference.identity_boundary: Biometric identity is not evaluated, verified, or claimed; review is limited to non-biometric visible appearance traits.

evaluation_policy.overall_target_pass_rule: Every target gate must pass from visible pixels; an ambiguous, cropped, merely implied, or partially present target fails.
evaluation_policy.gate_evidence_rule: Judge only visible objects, materials, spatial relations, contact, and photographic appearance. Do not infer satisfaction from the keyword, prompt, metadata, or filenames.

target_gates.observable_requirement: One coherent working environment visibly combines cream-and-turquoise enamel machinery, Bakelite or similarly molded analog controls, chrome or finned-aluminum housings, analog radiation gauges, and orbiting-electron or atomic starburst motifs. All cue families must be visibly present, not merely implied.

The location visibly reads as both reactor facility and greenhouse orchard in the same connected space: hydroponic vines bearing glowing cobalt-glass-like fruit, condensation or glass growing tubes, and reactor or radiation instrumentation must all be clearly visible.

The adult horticulturist is visibly calibrating a chrome seed-vault with believable hand-to-control contact while a compact analog robot simultaneously presents one glowing specimen in articulated tongs. The person, contact point, vault, robot, tongs, and specimen must each be readable.

The subject visibly wears a practical silver lamé work coverall and a clear acrylic dosimeter, while a bubble helmet is visibly stored or hanging within the worksite; these must read as functional atomic-age work gear rather than an unrelated fashion costume.

Atompunk cues visibly dominate at least three independent regions—architecture, machinery, and subject gear or props—so the image reads as a built mid-century atomic retrofuture without relying on a single emblem, isolated gadget, or written label.

confound_rejection_gates.observable_requirement: Reject a cyberpunk substitution: contemporary neon city streets, holographic interfaces, LED circuit armor, high-rise signage, or rain-soaked urban screens must not dominate; physical analog atomic-age equipment and the reactor greenhouse must remain visually primary.

Reject a steampunk or dieselpunk substitution: Victorian brass boilers, exposed clockwork, steam-driven machinery, soot-heavy interwar militarism, or riveted war engines must not dominate; clean enamel, chrome, Bakelite, analog nuclear science, and bubble-era forms must remain visually primary.

common_photo_reference_gates.observable_requirement: Exactly one primary adult woman is clearly visible, with coherent facial anatomy, two plausible hands, plausible fingers, and no duplicated, fused, or truncated body parts at the seed-vault interaction.

The primary adult's unobscured visible appearance carries the reference traits of long wavy dark hair, a gently oval face, warm brown eyes, natural straight-to-softly-arched brows, and softly defined coral lips. This gate compares only those visible traits and does not assess biometric identity.

The result visibly reads as one plausible photograph of a physically built set, with coherent depth, scale, reflections, condensation, glass, chrome, fabric, and contact shadows rather than an illustration, collage, or visibly synthetic object assembly.
